bluf: Grow Law is a founder led, law firm only growth agency (founded 2008, 95+ marketing experts, now on growlaw.co) selling SEO, GEO by practice area, PPC and lead attribution tied to signed cases in the client's CRM. It publishes hard, 163 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days, and sells AI visibility with a free report and ChatGPT advertising services, so the record points it at AI search for lawyers. A rival should know it sells paid search and runs no Google ads of its own, all 23 clients on record are names only, and the Monsoon read puts it at Landfall with displacement 80.6, a book buying on price.
doing:
The positioning line, a law firm only growth agency linking SEO, AI visibility, paid search and lead attribution to signed cases verified in the client's CRM, decodes as a legal search shop selling proof of cases rather than traffic. The headline claim is a typical 3.8x year one return and $50M+ qualified leads in six months, quoted as claims with no named client attached; the homepage also claims 160+ law firms served since 2008.

The sold mix leads with SEO, score 3: the homepage title and meta lead with lawyer SEO and case studies report large organic traffic gains. Four core lines score 2. AI Search / GEO: GEO pages per practice area plus a homepage AI visibility check. Data & Measurement: a Lead Attribution channel, calls scored and sourced, signed cases verified in the CRM and tied to spend. Paid Search: a PPC Ads Management service, with the KJT Law Group case reporting 440% more PPC qualified leads. Web & Product: Website Design pages, with the Cameron Law case built on a site revamp. CRO and Local score 1; content, social, email, programmatic and AI automation score 0. The services list adds Lead Generation, Advisory and ChatGPT Advertising Services. Proprietary: the Legal-Exclusive Growth System (Found, Qualified, Converted, Proven) and the Law Firm Academy. The record lists no partners.

AI posture: it sells GEO for each legal practice area with a free AI visibility report and lists ChatGPT advertising services.

Moves: none dated, no news, no case study titles and no jobs; the one recorded change is the domain, growlawfirm.com now resolving to growlaw.co, the same firm renamed and not a merger. Pricing: a public Pricing page is linked in the main nav, figures not captured, so the model is unknown rather than absent. Conspicuously absent for a legal lead generation agency: LSA evidence, any owned audience line, and any office or partner.
clients:
The ICP is SMB and the only vertical is Legal; the home market is the US, with no office listed.

The needs read holds 23 clients, 6 from case study pages and 17 from slugs, and codes all 23 N0, engagement named only: the results pages name the firms and the read captured nothing about the work. The capability notes add two observed signals: KJT Law Group reports 440% more PPC qualified leads, paid performance, and Cameron Law was built on a site revamp, web build and platform. The rest are named with no described work, their need inferred from what the agency leads with, organic demand through lawyer SEO with AI visibility behind it: Exceed Legal, The Ahearne Law Firm, Barr & Douds Attorneys and Lily Debrah Cruickshank & Associates from case study pages, and from slugs alone Omar Ochoa Law, Hagestad Law Group PLLC, Jacob Fuchsberg Law Firm, Texas Horizons Law Group, Yarborough Law Group, Newlin Law Offices, Gounaris Abboud, Rice Kendig, Lishman Law, Hodgson Law Office, Sequoia Legal, Stracci Law Group, SimVisa, Lehmbecker Law, Tauber Law, Kenneth J. Allen Law Group and Cohen & Malad; the GEO pages name the practice areas it sells into, PI, family, criminal and immigration.

No client is shared with another tracked agency, and the book is 23 of 23 names only.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places Grow Law best for KJ2, ads inside AI answers, and KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation. It is likely, moderate confidence, that these small law firms next want AI visibility by practice area tied to signed cases, the product it already sells, and roughly an even chance they ask for local service ads work the record shows it does not do (P3 absent), the KJ7 exposure.
house: Say and do: three lines tested. AI Search / GEO is corroborated: it publishes llms.txt and 17 AI topic URLs sit in its sitemap. Publishing cadence is corroborated: 163 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 175 in 365, from 293 URLs in total. Paid Search is contradicted: it sells PPC Ads Management and runs no Google ads of its own in the Transparency Center, the one gap the Radar lists. No AI crawlers are blocked. The tag stack shows gtm only, on Webflow, with no social pixels, no test tools and no ABM stack. Google ads: none. LinkedIn: 0 ads match the name query. Meta and TikTok: the record is silent. Channels listed: LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X and Facebook, a wide social footprint for a firm that buys no ads of its own.
market:
The Horus read scores Grow Law at 13.6 on the tailwind index, Favored band, percentile 55, say/do integrity 66.7. It is best placed for KJ2, ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them (net 0.269, Paid Search and AI Search / GEO), and KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation (net 0.202: AI Search / GEO and Paid Search positive, SEO negative). It is most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out (net -0.156, SEO and Paid Search), and KJ7, local discovery is being enclosed (net -0.052). Best scenario fit: The Walled Oasis at 54/100. P moves: making P1, P4 and P8, partial P6, unknown P5, absent P2, P3 and P7.

The Monsoon read: index 77.1, Landfall band, percentile 98, migration 73.6 against displacement 80.6, observed. The verdict says SEO (21) and Web & Product (14) carry the most movable hours and the shore split sends 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America; the SMB ICP term adds 12 points; no hub office or onshore claim is listed.
openings:
Lead with the paid search contradiction: Grow Law sells PPC Ads Management and cites 440% more PPC qualified leads for KJT Law Group, while the Transparency Center shows no Google ads of its own. A rival running its own visible legal PPC program very likely, moderate confidence, wins the proof argument. Falsifier: Google ads under its name appearing in the Transparency Center.

Price is the wider opening: displacement 80.6 on an observed Monsoon read says the book buys on price, SEO carries 21 of the movable hours, and the SMB ICP adds 12 points, so an offshore delivered rival can likely undercut it line by line. Its own Pricing page sits in the nav, figures not captured, so a rival publishing outcome pricing for signed cases meets it on ground it chose.

The contestable accounts are all 23 names, since none has described work. Local is the gap to attack: Local scores 1, P3 is absent with no LSA evidence, and KJ7 is a headwind, so a rival leading with local service ads and map pack work for small firms likely takes the local budget, low confidence on how much of it Grow Law currently holds.

Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users versus search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

Indicator I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would test the value of the Pricing page it already publishes.
